- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.67) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects; dampen next period’s forecast.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum direction.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 3–5 days, model underperforms; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast.
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong moves; if price deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust toward average.
